chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I was with Isa ibn Musa when a thief was brought to him, and a man from the family of Umar was present. The man turned to me and asked, so I said: 'What do you say about the thief if he confesses to himself that he stole?' He said: 'His hand is cut off.' I said: 'And what do you say about the fornicator if he confesses to himself four times?' He said: 'We stone him.' I said: 'What prevents you from cutting off the hand of the thief if he confesses to himself twice, so that he is in the same status as the fornicator?'

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: In the status of / equivalent to
key_terms.يُقْطَع: He is cut off (amputation of the hand)

ai.seo_question: How many confessions are required for the punishment of theft in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential nuance that two separate confessions are required for the hadd punishment of theft, distinguishing it from the four confessions needed for fornication. The narrator, Aban ibn Uthman, engages with the jurist Isa ibn Musa to challenge the apparent inconsistency, highlighting the scholarly debate on whether a single confession suffices or if distinct procedural safeguards apply to each crime. This exchange underscores the Shia emphasis on precise evidentiary standards in applying corporal punishments.
